name: get_scene_info
description: Blender version, file, frame range/fps, render engine and resolution, active camera, collections, and every object (name, type, location, rotation in degrees, scale, dimensions, materials).

name: get_object_info
description: Details of one object: transform, mesh stats, modifiers, materials, keyframes, children.

name: create_object
description: Create an object: cube, plane, sphere, ico_sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, circle, grid, monkey, text, empty, camera, or a light (point, sun, spot, area). Meters and degrees. Cameras become the scene camera by default.

size.description: Overall size/diameter in meters (text: letter height). Default 2 (text 1).

color.description: "#rrggbb": quick material for meshes/text, or light color.

active.description: Camera: make it the scene camera. Default true.

look_at.description: Camera/light/empty: aim at an object name or [x, y, z].

collection.description: Put it in this collection (created if missing).

name: modify_object
description: Change an object: location, move_by, rotation (degrees), scale, dimensions, look_at, parent ("" to clear), hidden, shade smooth/flat, text, light energy/color, camera lens/active, select, apply_transform, new_name.

name: duplicate_object
description: Duplicate an object count times, each shifted by offset (meters).

name: set_material
description: Create or edit a Principled BSDF material on an object: color, metallic, roughness, emission (+ strength), transmission (glass), alpha, image texture. Reuses the object's current material unless material/new is given.

image.description: Image file for the base color.

append.description: Add as an extra slot instead of replacing.

name: add_modifier
description: Add a modifier (BEVEL, SUBSURF, ARRAY, MIRROR, SOLIDIFY, BOOLEAN, DISPLACE, WIREFRAME, SCREW, CURVE, ...) with settings by their Python names, e.g. {"levels": 2}, {"width": 0.05, "segments": 3}, {"count": 5, "relative_offset_displace": [1.2, 0, 0]}, {"operation": "DIFFERENCE", "object": "Cutter"}. apply=true applies it.

name: animate
description: Keyframe an object property: location, rotation (degrees), scale, or for lights/cameras energy, color, lens. keyframes = [{frame, value}]. Optional interpolation (BEZIER, LINEAR, CONSTANT), frame_start/frame_end/fps, clear=true to remove animation.

name: set_world
description: World background: solid color or an HDRI image, and strength.

name: render_settings
description: Set engine (eevee, cycles, workbench), resolution [w, h], percentage, samples, fps, frame_start/frame_end, transparent background, output path, format (PNG, JPEG, OPEN_EXR, MP4), view_transform (Standard, AgX, Filmic). Returns current settings (call with no args to read).

name: viewport_screenshot
description: Screenshot the 3D Viewport and return it as an image (fast way to see the scene). Optional view (FRONT, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM, CAMERA) and frame_selected to zoom to everything.

name: render_preview
description: Quick low-sample render through the scene camera, returned as an image. Render settings are restored afterwards.

name: render
description: Full render of the current frame (or the animation) with the scene's settings to path / the output path.

path.description: Output path. For animation, a prefix like D:/out/frame_ or a .mp4 with format MP4.

name: import_file
description: Import obj, fbx, glb/gltf, stl, ply, usd, abc, svg, or an image (as a textured plane).

size.description: Image plane size in meters. Default 2.

name: export_file
description: Export the scene (or only the named objects) to obj, fbx, glb, gltf, stl, ply or usd.

name: file
description: save (optionally Save As path), open a .blend, or new (default startup scene; empty=true for a blank one).

name: undo
description: Undo (or redo) steps. Each modifying MCP call is one step.

name: run_python
description: Escape hatch: run Python in Blender (bpy, mathutils, math, C = context, D = data, plus get_obj, describe, hex_color, run_op, ctx). Returns the last expression's value (or a variable named result) and printed output. Use run_op(bpy.ops.x.y, ...) for operators that need a UI context.
